16 OCTOBER 2026 · IMPLEMENTATION AND VERIFICATION

Less repetition. More room for photos.

Implemented the layout fixes from the current interface comparison. Existing work, processing definitions, project compatibility, photo edits, captured operation inputs and native import/export adapters were retained. No commit, push, signing change or publication.

FindingImplemented
Mac batch overflowResize uses bounded compact property rows and numeric fields. Framing, Rotate & Flip and canvas appearance are disclosed. Auto-framing buttons stack instead of demanding a wide horizontal row. Mac’s remaining native forms use grouped layout.
Thumbnail clutter and operation scopeSmall stack markers replace repeated two-line labels. Accessibility identifies operation membership, selection and active photo separately. Count stays visible; fixed-input details open from Info and inputs change through the photo-stack menu. Standalone settings sheets retain their own scope header.
Repeated headings and mobile controlsiOS uses the native task heading once. Compact batch shows the count instead of repeating Batch Edit. Browse/Frame/Compare moves into View options on iPhone. One Batch Settings button replaces duplicate entry points; Rotate/Refine are in the focused-photo menu.
Batch property densityBatch Adjust and Resize use the same compact controls as photo properties. Mixed-value explanations remain available and field edits remain sparse. Adjacent iPad properties no longer repeat the operation summary.
Portrait iPadPersistent batch properties require landscape and at least 1000 points of detail width; otherwise the toolbar opens a settings sheet. Large text avoids the permanent column. Refine Framing uses full-screen presentation when no persistent inspector is visible.
Document and navigation chromeMac/iPad photo tabs, Workspace, history, Edits and Original share one document bar. Tab filenames truncate in the middle and retain full accessible names and hover help. Mac photo properties identify the active tool. Presets and Help & Review collapse in the sidebar.
Finishing detailsSearch uses a concise prompt with an accessible explanation. Favourite buttons are optional; existing favourites remain marked, and context/accessibility actions remain available. Fit/actual-pixel entry shows its current mode. Action labels handle singular photo counts.

Before and after

Both columns use native hosted captures of synthetic local sources at matching review viewports. Before is from the preceding comparison; after is from the final native test runs. These are not physical-device screenshots. Mac omits its native title-bar toolbar. The iPad browsing fixture still has a sidebar-edge capture artefact; no claim is made that this artefact was repaired.
